A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Kuramoto Orientation Diffusion Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison; retained material can be matched across pagination and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments, Earth/climate density-modeling results, ablations, and Navier–Stokes spectral evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds results for coupled fluid dynamics and conditional Navier–Stokes forecasting.

M1.justification: V1's fluid extension diffuses log-amplitude independently of locally coupled phases. V2 introduces reciprocal amplitude–phase coupling during early diffusion (Eq. 21), and conditional score training with classifier-free guidance for forecasting (Eq. 22). These substantially extend the procedure; the original variant remains as 'Naive' in Table 9.

E1.justification: All datasets are retained. Appendix B.4 adds one-step Navier–Stokes forecasting from two historical frames alongside unconditional generation, extending task coverage within the existing fluid domain.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds SGM in Cartesian coordinates, also used in the new forecasting comparison. V1's SGM (VP-SDE) comparator is retained as SGM (Amplitude-Phase Decomposition), with identical scores. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new forecasting evaluation conditions on two historical states and measures one-step velocity prediction using MSE. Existing image and Earth/climate protocols, and the unconditional fluid spectral metrics and fitting interval, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds a comparison testing reciprocal amplitude–phase coupling against the original uncoupled-channel variant. Figures 10–11 add spectral-shape inspection and two forecasting case studies. The existing Brodatz coupling ablation and alternative-metric analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Table 8 retains the same five-run averaging and uncertainty values. The added fluid results provide point estimates without introducing repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 9 retains the original scores and adds slope-difference/Wasserstein results of 0.5590/0.0029 for Cartesian SGM and 0.3343/0.0005 for coupled Kuramoto. New Table 10 reports forecasting MSE of 0.0260 versus 0.0188, respectively. These are additional variant/task results, not revisions to the old model's scores; other benchmark results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 revises the mathematical definition of the fluid stochastic process to include cross-channel interactions and defines guided conditional scores. The mean-field, local score-matching, and Fourier derivations in Appendix A remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central synchronization-based generative contribution and headline image-performance claims are retained. V2 foregrounds Earth/climate and fluid applicability in the introduction, but v1 already claimed this three-domain applicability in Section 3.1 and reported the corresponding appendix experiments.

C2.justification: V2 explains how phase coherence promotes amplitude growth, how amplitude strengthens synchronization, and why cross-channel coupling is disabled late in diffusion. It interprets the new comparisons as supporting joint amplitude–phase modeling and forecasting as testing temporal dynamics. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The fluid extension documents condition-dropout training, the coupling cutoff t < T/alpha, and guidance parameter omega. Numerical values for alpha, omega, and the dropout probability are not supplied. Existing optimizer, architecture, hardware, schedules, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ho and Salimans's Classifier-free Diffusion Guidance and cites it for conditional inference. The remaining cited works and the positioning relative to geometric generative models and neural oscillations are unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the introductory experiment summary, expands B.4 under unconditional-generation and conditional-forecasting headings, and adds acknowledgments. It also shortens the generic broader-impact discussion. The overall organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 9, adds Table 10 and Figures 10–11, and relocates the unchanged SNR figure from page 8 to page 9. The original appendix sample grids are retained as Figures 12–15. These are localized display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V1's fluid comparison used only amplitude-phase SGM. V2 adds a Cartesian baseline and a coupled-versus-uncoupled comparison, making the evidence for amplitude–phase interaction more informative. The forecasting experiment additionally tests conditional accuracy beyond unconditional spectral realism. These targeted gains improve the paper, although missing numerical coupling/guidance/dropout settings and uncertainty reporting limit the strength and reproducibility of the new evidence.
